blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A shared library has `List<Order> byDate(List<Order> orders)`, which sorts its argument in place and returns it. A service calls it with `orders.stream().filter(Order::isOpen).toList()` and gets UnsupportedOperationException. What should change?

options.text: The library should return a new sorted list, since List allows a list to refuse the element writes that sorting in place needs
options.says: set and the other mutators are optional operations of List; a method typed to take any List can't rely on them, so it builds a new list

options.text: The library should return a new sorted list after catching the exception, since a list that refuses those writes breaks the contract of List
options.says: throwing UnsupportedOperationException from a mutator is part of List's contract, so the list keeps it; the method assumed a promise List never made

options.text: The service should pass a different list, since toList() refuses a call that List requires every list to accept
options.says: the javadoc marks the mutators optional, so refusing them keeps List's contract; the code in breach is the one relying on them

options.text: The service should pass a different list, since a list built by a stream allows element writes and this one must come from elsewhere
options.says: stream().toList() returns an unmodifiable list, as the page's run shows

origin.section: List's Mutators Are Optional Operations, So the Caller That Changes Its Argument Is in Breach

questions.stem: A rate limiter skips clients for which `exempt.contains(apiKey)` is true; `apiKey` is null for anonymous requests. A cleanup changes `exempt` from `Arrays.asList(keys)` to `Set.of(keys)`, and every test sends an API key. What happens on the first anonymous request?

options.text: It is rate-limited as before, since contains lets any collection answer false for an element it doesn't hold
options.says: Collection.contains may throw NullPointerException for a null query on a collection that doesn't permit nulls; Set.of does

options.text: It is rate-limited as before, since Set.of lets a null query through as a key it holds no entry for
options.says: Set.of throws NullPointerException for contains(null), as the page states beside the List.of run and in its Reference table

options.text: It fails with NullPointerException, since Collection lets an implementation that holds no nulls refuse a null query
options.says: the NullPointerException is marked optional in Collection.contains, so Set.of keeps the contract and the code that passes null is the one exposed

options.text: It fails with NullPointerException, since Set.of refuses a query that Collection requires every set to answer
options.says: the javadoc allows the exception, so Set.of keeps the contract; the caller relied on a promise Collection doesn't make

origin.section: List's Mutators Are Optional Operations, So the Caller That Changes Its Argument Is in Breach

questions.stem: A billing job adds each invoice's billing time to a `HashSet<Date>` to count billing moments. Invoices from the API carry `new Date(ms)`; the same invoice from the nightly import carries `rs.getTimestamp("billed_at")` for the same millisecond. One run reads the API first, the next run reads the import first. How many elements does that moment add?

options.text: One in both runs, since the two values hold the same milliseconds and have the same hashCode
options.says: the hash codes match, but Timestamp.equals refuses a Date, so the outcome depends on which value the set asks

options.text: Two in both runs, since a Timestamp and a Date are never equal to each other
options.says: Date.equals accepts a Timestamp of the same millisecond; only Timestamp.equals refuses a Date

options.text: Two when the API comes first and one when the import comes first, since the set asks the value being added
options.says: adding the Timestamp after the Date asks Timestamp.equals, which says false; adding the Date after the Timestamp asks Date.equals, which says true

options.text: One when the API comes first and two when the import comes first, since the set asks the value already stored
options.says: a HashSet calls equals on the element being added, as the page's run shows: app first gives 2, db first gives 1

origin.section: Timestamp Breaks the Symmetry Object.equals Promises, So a Set of Dates Depends on Arrival Order

questions.stem: Checkout calls `rate.cents(grams)` through an interface whose javadoc says: `grams` is any weight from 0 up; the result is a price in cents, 0 or more. A new carrier's implementation is proposed. Which version can be handed to checkout in place of the existing ones?

options.text: One that throws for parcels over 30 kg, since the carrier can't ship them and checkout should hear about it
options.says: it rejects weights the interface says every implementation accepts, a strengthened precondition that fails checkout at run time

options.text: One that returns -1 for parcels over 30 kg, since checkout can treat a negative price as a refusal
options.says: it returns outside the promised range, a weakened postcondition; code written against the interface treats -1 as a price, as checkout treated FlatCoupon's 500 on a 300 cart

options.text: One that also takes a negative weight and prices it at 0, since checkout never sends a negative weight
options.says: accepting more and keeping the promised range leaves every caller's assumption true; no caller written against the interface depends on negative weights failing

options.text: One that takes only whole kilograms and throws for other weights, since checkout rounds weights before calling
options.says: the interface accepts any weight, so a caller written against it may pass 1,250 g; the override strengthens the precondition

origin.section: A Subtype May Accept More and Promise More, Never Less

concepts: Collection.contains may throw NullPointerException for a null query on a collection that holds no nulls, as List.of and Set.of do, while ArrayList answers false.
